title: Auslander–Buchsbaum depth formula
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring (a ring with exactly one maximal ideal) [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $M$ be a nonzero finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] of finite projective dimension [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. Then $$\operatorname{depth}(R)=\operatorname{pd}_R(M)+\operatorname{depth}(M),$$ where depths are taken with respect to $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-depth].

proof.text: First justify induction on the depth of the module, uniformly over all Noetherian local rings. Nakayama gives $\mathfrak mM\ne M$, since $M$ is finite and nonzero and the Jacobson radical of a local ring is its unique maximal ideal. If $\operatorname{depth}(M)=0$ it is already finite. Otherwise the supremum definition of depth supplies a regular sequence of positive length in $\mathfrak m$; its first element $y$ is injective on $M$. The depth-drop lemma applied to $y$ explicitly says that $\operatorname{depth}(M)$ is a finite integer. Thus put $t=\operatorname{depth}(M)\in\mathbf N$ and use strong induction on $t$ for the asserted formula for every pair $(R,M)$ satisfying the hypotheses.

Put $e=\operatorname{pd}_R(M)$. By the resolution-length definition, part (2) of the projective-dimension well-definedness lemma, and the minimal finite free resolution lemma choose an exact resolution $0\to F_e\to\cdots\to F_0\to M\to0$ with $F_i=R^{n_i}$ and every differential between free terms having entries in $\mathfrak m$. If $e>0$, $n_e>0$: otherwise deleting the zero top term gives a shorter projective resolution, contradicting the definition of $e$. If $e=0$, $F_0\cong M$ and $n_0>0$ since $M\ne0$.

A nonzero finite free module $R^n$, $n>0$, has the same depth as $R$: quotienting coordinatewise by each prefix of a sequence gives $(R/J)^n$, multiplication is injective on this module exactly when it is injective on $R/J$, and $(R/J)^n\ne0$ exactly when $R/J\ne0$. Therefore the regular sequences, and hence their length suprema, coincide. For $e=0$ this proves the desired formula immediately. For $e>0$ define $Z_0=M$ and $Z_i=\operatorname{im}(F_i\to F_{i-1})$ for $1\le i\le e$, identifying $Z_e$ with $F_e$. Exactness gives $0\to Z_{i+1}\to F_i\to Z_i\to0$ for $0\le i<e$. Each $Z_i$ is finite by the Noetherian-submodule lemma (and $Z_0$ is finite by hypothesis). Each is nonzero: $Z_i=0$, $i\ge1$, would allow truncation to a projective resolution of $M$ of length at most $i-1<e$. Consequently every $F_i$ in these sequences is nonzero too. These checks ensure that all three modules in every application of the depth lemma are nonzero finite modules.

For $e>0$ apply the exact-free-complex last-minors lemma to the unaugmented free complex. Its top rank $n_e$ is positive. Every $n_e$-minor of the top matrix is a sum of products of $n_e$ entries in $\mathfrak m$, so the ideal $I$ of these minors is contained in $\mathfrak m$ and cannot equal $R$. The lemma therefore supplies an $R$-regular sequence of length $e$ in $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. The depth definition gives $d:=\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge e$. In particular $d>0$; the depth-drop lemma applied to the first element of this regular sequence shows that $d$ is finite.

Base case $t=0$, with $e>0$. Start with $\operatorname{depth}(Z_e)=d$. In $0\to Z_{i+1}\to F_i\to Z_i\to0$ the second inequality of the depth lemma gives $\operatorname{depth}(Z_i)\ge\min\{d,\operatorname{depth}(Z_{i+1})-1\}$. Descending induction from $i=e-1$ to $i=0$ yields $\operatorname{depth}(Z_i)\ge d-(e-i)$, because $d\ge e$ and $\operatorname{depth}(F_i)=d$. If a syzygy has infinite depth its contribution to the minimum is $d$, so the same bound remains valid. Hence $0=t=\operatorname{depth}(Z_0)\ge d-e$. Together with $d\ge e$ this gives $d=e=e+t$.

Induction step $t>0$, with $e>0$. The split short exact sequence $0\to R\to R\oplus M\to M\to0$ has nonzero finite terms. The first inequality of the depth lemma gives $\operatorname{depth}(R\oplus M)\ge\min\{d,t\}>0$. Nakayama ensures $\mathfrak m(R\oplus M)\ne R\oplus M$, so the depth definition supplies a regular sequence of positive length on $R\oplus M$ in $\mathfrak m$. Let $x$ be its first term. Multiplication by $x$ is injective on each summand, so $x$ is a common nonzerodivisor on $R$ and $M$.

Set $S=R/xR$ and $N=M/xM$. The depth-drop lemma gives $N\ne0$. The ring $S$ is nonzero local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/xR$: its maximal ideals correspond to maximal ideals of $R$ containing $xR$, and $x\in\mathfrak m$. It is Noetherian since every ideal of $S$ is the image of an ideal of $R$, whose finite generators map to generators; $N$ is finite since generators of $M$ descend. Reduction of the resolution modulo $x$ remains exact, as follows explicitly. In each $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ of Step 3, multiplication by $x$ is injective on $C$: for $C=M$ this was proved in Step 6, and the other $C$ are submodules of finite free modules, on which $x$ is injective because it is injective on $R$. If $a\in A$ becomes zero in $B/xB$, write $a=xb$; the image of $b$ in $C$ is killed by $x$, hence is zero, so $b\in A$ and $a\in xA$. To check exactness in the middle, if $b\in B$ maps to $xc$ in $C$, lift $c$ to $b_1\in B$ and observe that $b-xb_1\in A$. Surjectivity follows by lifting representatives. Thus $0\to A/xA\to B/xB\to C/xC\to0$ is exact. Splicing these sequences gives $0\to S^{n_e}\to\cdots\to S^{n_0}\to N\to0$. Its differential entries still lie in the maximal ideal of $S$ and $n_e>0$.

The reduced resolution has shortest possible length $e$, not merely length at most $e$. Indeed let $k=S/(\mathfrak m/xR)$. Finite free modules are flat by the finite-free flatness lemma, so the flat-resolution Tor comparison applied to the reduced resolution, extended by zero above $e$, identifies $\operatorname{Tor}^S_e(N,k)$ with its degree-$e$ tensor homology. Tensoring a free term $S^n$ with $k$ gives $k^n$ by sending the basis vectors to the standard coordinate vectors; all differential entries become zero. Hence this homology is $k^{n_e}\ne0$. If $q=\operatorname{pd}_S(N)<e$, part (2) of the projective-dimension well-definedness lemma and the minimal finite free resolution lemma would give a finite free resolution of $N$ of length $q$. Its terms are again flat, and the same Tor comparison computes $\operatorname{Tor}^S_e(N,k)=0$ since its degree-$e$ term is zero. This contradiction proves $\operatorname{pd}_S(N)=e$. All resolutions used here are augmented exact complexes of modules, so their augmentations induce an isomorphism on degree-zero homology and have zero higher homology, exactly the hypothesis of the comparison theorem.

Apply the depth-drop lemma to $x$ on $R$ and on $M$: as $R$-module depths, $\operatorname{depth}_R(S)=d-1$ and $\operatorname{depth}_R(N)=t-1$. The depth-over-quotient-ring lemma, for the ideal $xR\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and the modules $S,N$ annihilated by it, identifies these with $\operatorname{depth}(S)$ and $\operatorname{depth}_S(N)$ respectively. Step 7 verified that $S$ is Noetherian local and $N$ is finite nonzero; Step 8 verified finite projective dimension $e$. Strong induction, uniform over rings, therefore applies to $(S,N)$ at depth $t-1<t$ and gives $d-1=e+(t-1)$. Since $d,t$ are finite integers, adding one proves $d=e+t$. Together with the free case and the depth-zero case this completes the induction.
